answer: Yes. Aschenbach’s creative drive is metaphorically rendered as an internal “produzierendes Triebwerk,” suggesting both disciplined productivity and mechanical exhaustion. The reference to Cicero’s “motus animi continuus” gives his artistic restlessness a classical framework, while biblical inscriptions and apocalyptic beasts introduce mortality and spiritual mystery. His vision of a luxuriant yet unhealthy wilderness deepens the tension between desire and danger.
